newsitem.title: USA: Broward County, Fla., school chief survives vote.
newsitem.headline: Broward County, Fla., school chief survives vote.

text.p: Broward County, Fla., school Superintendent Frank Petruzielo narrowly survived a confidence vote prompted in part by investigations into the district's construction program.

The county school board gave Petruzielo a 4-3 confidence vote Tuesday, the Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel said. The vote was called by school board member Lois Wexler, who has accused the superintendnet of cutting corners on competitive bidding.

Wexler and other critics on the board alleged that Petruzielo withheld information from board members, rebid a computer contract after they had accepted a different vendor, and generally ignored board members' wishes.

Petruzielo did not respond directly to the allegations but said he had been made a scapegoat for problems such as school crowding. The Sun-Sentinel quoted him as saying the confidence vote was "an effort to weaken me and avoid a costly buyout."
Criticism of the superintendent has intensified amid a state grand jury investigation and a federal probe of the school district's building program.
